entities.summary:
Joseph Leonz Andermatt (died 1817) was a pivotal Swiss military leader whose career spanned the tumultuous transition from the Old Swiss Confederacy to the French-backed Helvetic Republic and beyond. A seasoned mercenary captain, Andermatt initially served in the Swiss Guards for France, a common path for ambitious Swiss officers, before returning to his homeland to play a central, if controversial, role in the internal and external conflicts that reshaped Switzerland during the French Revolutionary Wars. His actions, particularly in suppressing federalist revolts and commanding nascent Helvetic forces against formidable foreign armies, underscore the profound impact of revolutionary ideals and external pressures on traditional Swiss neutrality and political structures at the turn of the 19th century.

Andermatt's most significant period of activity commenced with the French invasion of Switzerland in 1798, which led to the collapse of the Old Confederacy and the establishment of the centralized Helvetic Republic. He quickly rose to prominence within the new regime's military, commanding troops against counter-revolutionary forces and federalist insurgents, most notably during the Stecklikrieg of 1802, where he led government forces in a largely unsuccessful attempt to quell a widespread federalist uprising. He also played a crucial role in the Second Coalition War, commanding Helvetic brigades alongside French forces against Austrian and Russian armies on Swiss soil, including engagements around Zurich. His leadership was instrumental in the early attempts to forge a unified Swiss national army, moving away from the canton-based militia system of the past.
